items.headline: Cabinet clears US$30m OPEC Fund loan
items.summary: Cabinet approved a US$30 million policy-based loan from the OPEC Fund to back the 'Reforms for Growth, Resilience and Openness' programme, alongside World Bank financing under the same operation.

items.headline: GMOA threatens tougher action after Nov 30
items.summary: The doctors' union says the 2027 Budget treats doctors unfairly and is running a week-long awareness campaign over salary deductions. It warns of protests or strikes if the government does not respond by November 30.

items.headline: University non-academic staff strike tomorrow
items.summary: University non-academic workers will hold a one-day symbolic strike on November 25 over cuts to allowances and privileges, and plan a two-day strike on December 1–2 if the issue is not resolved.

items.headline: Teachers plan sick-leave protest on Nov 30
items.summary: Teachers' and principals' unions will report sick on November 30 to press for the remaining two-thirds of their promised salary increase. One faction of the Lanka Teachers' Service Union is staying out.

items.headline: ADB approves US$200m for small businesses
items.summary: The Asian Development Bank approved a US$200 million package to help SMEs get credit. Half goes to loans through partner lenders, including US$40 million for green projects, and half is a policy loan to strengthen credit guarantees, reporting and microfinance oversight.

items.headline: Marikkar questions Foreign Employment Bureau hires
items.summary: SJB MP S. M. Marikkar told Parliament that several appointees at the Bureau of Foreign Employment lack the required qualifications. He also accused the Deputy Minister's private secretary of interfering in the bureau.

items.headline: Deputy minister: pay demands show trust in govt
items.summary: A health deputy minister said the wave of salary demands reflects public trust that the current government will deliver.

items.headline: Sajith urges merit-based cricket selection
items.summary: Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa told Parliament that players should be picked on runs and wickets, not vague factors like team spirit, and warned against favouritism based on school, family or region.

items.headline: UK to help reform Sri Lanka Customs
items.summary: Sri Lanka Customs signed an MoU to receive technical assistance from the United Kingdom as part of a new reform push.

items.headline: US$5.1m insulin and blood-thinner contracts
items.summary: Cabinet approved drug deals worth about US$5.1 million: India's M.J. Biopharm will supply about 2.7 million insulin vials, and China's Shenzhen Techdow will supply around 920,000 enoxaparin doses.

items.headline: India grants Rs. 600m for Puttalam Hospital
items.summary: India will provide Rs. 600 million to develop the Puttalam hospital.

items.headline: Kurunegala–Galewela expressway work starts Dec 1
items.summary: Building the Kurunegala–Galewela section of the Central Expressway starts on December 1. The project will take about 3.5 years, cost over Rs. 240 billion and be paid for from domestic funds, without foreign loans.

items.headline: Colombo shares close lower
items.summary: The ASPI and S&P SL20 both ended Tuesday in the red on turnover of just over Rs. 1.1 billion. John Keells Holdings slipped 1.6%.

items.headline: Fake 'British national' held over gold thefts
items.summary: Fort Police arrested a man who allegedly posed as a British national and stole nearly Rs. 2 million worth of gold jewellery from Colombo shops between September and November. Heroin was also found on him.

items.headline: 284 environmental officers to be recruited
items.summary: The government will recruit 284 environmental officers to fill vacancies across the island.

items.headline: US Embassy shut for two days for Thanksgiving
items.summary: The US Embassy in Colombo will close for two days for the Thanksgiving holiday.

items.headline: Amber lightning warning for 24 districts
items.summary: The Met Department warned of a high chance of thunderstorms and lightning this evening and tonight in every district except Jaffna. The warning is valid until 11 PM.

items.headline: Air quality improves sharply
items.summary: The Central Environmental Authority says the Air Quality Index has fallen from nearly 200 to around 50 now that smoke drifting in from India has cleared.

items.headline: Supermoon visible tonight
items.summary: A supermoon will be visible over Sri Lanka tonight.

items.headline: Ireland set up final with SL women tomorrow
items.summary: Ireland beat the Netherlands by 44 runs and will meet Sri Lanka in the ICC Women's Emerging Nations Trophy final in the UAE on Wednesday.

items.headline: Wakeel wins Mumbai squash title
items.summary: Shamil Wakeel won the PSA Satellite squash event in Mumbai, and fellow Sri Lankan Tuwin Osanda Herath finished third.
